text:
B: Hi. Gemma.
A: Hello. Gillian. Sorry, the laptop's on the island, it's at a funny angle.
B: You're fine. Nice kitchen.
A: Thank you. Had it redone two years ago. Erm, do you know what they're actually doing with all this? The ratings and that?
B: No idea. First impressions, I think. Whether they match up.
A: Mm. I'd just like to know who's looking at it.
B: Fair.
A: So, erm... where are you?
B: Basingstoke. Chineham.
A: Oh, the other lady was Chineham. Laura?
B: Was she? Didn't know that. Haven't had her yet. Where are you?
A: Bramhall. Stockport. It's a nice area, South Manchester. I'm an optometrist, in Stockport town centre, three days a week.
B: Oh, eyes. Do you like it?
A: The clinical bit's fine. It's the selling I can't stand. They've got targets now for frames, coatings, anti-glare, the lot, and the manager hovers about while you're trying to tell someone they've got early glaucoma. It's not what I trained for, do you know what I mean? I trained to look after people's eyes, not to flog them a blue-light filter they don't need.
B: I sell cars. New cars. So I'm probably the manager in that story.
A: Oh. Right.
B: I just mean, to be fair, someone's got to pay for the building, yeah? If the customer's happy and you've told them the truth, I don't see the problem with an add-on.
A: Well. It depends if they need it.
B: Sure.
A: Erm, yeah. That's it really.
B: Do you do Saturdays?
A: No. And I'm not going to. They keep hinting, but I've done my time with Saturdays.
B: I do alternate ones. I don't mind them, Saturday's where the money is.
A: I suppose in your job, yeah.
B: Is that your dog? Bottom of the screen?
A: Bella. Cockapoo. She's flat out. She needs her nails doing and the groomer wants forty-five pound for a full groom, which I think is daylight robbery.
B: Haggle. Honestly. Say you'll go somewhere else.
A: I did, actually. Got five off.
B: There you go. I've got a spaniel, Dexter. He rolled in fox poo this morning on the walk, so that was my seven o'clock sorted.
A: Oh, God. Bella did that once at Bramhall Park. Never again.
B: Stinks for days.
A: Days. Martin wouldn't let her in the lounge. Erm, have you got kids?
B: No.
A: Right.
B: Just Dexter. And my husband's building a garden room, so that's basically a child.
A: Ha. Our neighbours had an extension done and it's blocked all the light in the side of the kitchen. They didn't even ask. Well, they had planning, but they didn't ask us. I'm still annoyed about it, if I'm honest.
B: Did you object?
A: Martin said leave it. I should've objected.
B: You should've. I'd have been round there.
A: That's what I said. Anyway. What are you doing for tea tonight, then? Sorry, dinner.
B: Chicken and rice. Craig does the cooking. Friday's a takeaway.
A: Indian?
B: Indian or Nando's.
A: Indian, us. Same place every week. I'm not fussed about trying new places, I like what I like.
B: Same. I don't do those places with tiny portions on a slate.
A: Oh, no. Slates. Give it me on a plate, I'm not a goat.
B: Ha. Yeah.
A: Erm, do you get away much?
B: Twice a year. Tenerife, Turkey. I always ask for an upgrade at check-in. Nine times out of ten you get one if you complain properly.
A: I'm the same with refunds. If something's wrong, I say so. People don't, and then they moan after.
B: Exactly. You just have to be—
